evals.prompt: Our FastAPI app on Azure Functions Flex has Easy Auth enabled. A v2 delegated token has the correct tenant, API client GUID audience, and access_as_user scope, but both /.auth/me and /v1/openapi.json return 403 before any FastAPI logs appear. Diagnose this without exposing the token and propose the smallest authsettingsV2 Bicep correction.
evals.expected_output: A layered diagnosis that distinguishes token issuance, JWT validity, Easy Auth authentication, and Easy Auth authorization, identifies the azp client allowlist as the likely 403 cause, and gives a safe Bicep and negative-test matrix.
expectations: Separates token issuance, JWT validity, Easy Auth authentication, and Easy Auth authorization.
Explains that defaultAuthorizationPolicy.allowedApplications evaluates azp for v2 or appid for v1 and is separate from preAuthorizedApplications.
Uses safe claim booleans rather than printing or persisting the bearer token.
Includes an explicit matrix with no-token 401, wrong-audience 401 as an empirical control, unauthorized-client 403, and authorized-token 200.
The Bicep correction adds only the approved caller client ID from azp to allowedApplications and does not broaden allowed audiences.

evals.prompt: Design authentication for a FastAPI API hosted on Azure App Service. It has a browser UI with user context, a scheduled Azure-hosted worker, and an external CI integration. Explain delegated vs managed identity vs app-only, define the Entra registrations and consent boundaries, and show a secure authsettingsV2 Bicep shape.
evals.expected_output: A flow decision matrix, durable resource API and caller relationships, least-privilege consent guidance, and parameterized Easy Auth configuration with correct issuer, audiences, and client authorization.
expectations: Uses delegated authorization for user-context browser requests, managed identity for the Azure-hosted worker, and app-only credentials or federation for external CI.
Explicitly rejects delegated Azure CLI user tokens for unattended production automation and selects managed identity for Azure-hosted work or federation/certificates for external CI.
Keeps custom API scopes and app roles distinct from Microsoft Graph permissions.
Uses a tenant/version-correct issuer and only audiences belonging to the resource API.

evals.prompt: Create an azd smoke-test plan for a FastAPI Azure Functions Flex deployment protected by Easy Auth and private data services. We keep hitting provider, region, OneDeploy, 401, and 403 failures. Give a read-only preflight, deployment sequence, safe diagnostics, cleanup boundaries, and a report format that proves each layer separately.
evals.expected_output: A sequenced, evidence-driven plan that separates infrastructure and deployment failures from authentication, authorization, FastAPI, and business-layer proof.
expectations: Checks Flex region support and Microsoft.App registration for VNet integration before provisioning.
Distinguishes provision and OneDeploy failures from HTTP authentication failures.
Preserves durable app registrations and consent while cleaning only explicitly owned transient resources.
Reports token, platform authentication, FastAPI, and business or database proof separately with an explicit live, local static, documented, or empirical evidence label.
